Links: [{"title":"Bug: Hydration mismatch on `<script defer>` rendered inside `<head>` · Issue #36169 · facebook/react · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/36169"},{"title":"Bug: Scripts injected by browser extensions (e.g. React dev tools) may cause hydration errors · Issue #25924 · facebook/react · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924"},{"title":"Hydration Error in Next.js 15 with React 19 Due to cz-shortcut-listen=\"true\" Attribute Injection from Colorzilla Extension · vercel/next.js · Discussion #72035 · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035"},{"title":"Bug: Hydration mismatch error due to plugins generating script tag on top · Issue #24430 · facebook/react · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/24430"},{"title":"React 19 hydration error ignoring · Issue #15886 · getsentry/sentry-javascript · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-javascript/issues/15886"},{"title":"React hydration error in Next.js development server · Issue #1255 · igrigorik/videospeed · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/igrigorik/videospeed/issues/1255"},{"title":"Bug: A tree hydrated but some attributes of the server rendered HTML didn't match the client properties. · Issue #35210 · facebook/react · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/35210"},{"title":"Fix browser extension hydration mismatch by suv27 · Pull Request #26 · suv27/Layer7-Siege · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/suv27/Layer7-Siege/pull/26"},{"title":"Fix hydration mismatch from browser extensions · Issue #2 · himan243/LeetTrack · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/himan243/LeetTrack/issues/2"},{"title":"Would it be possible to run Hydrogen with React 19 beta? · Shopify/hydrogen · Discussion #2062 · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/Shopify/hydrogen/discussions/2062"}]

The search turned up several relevant GitHub threads, mostly about extensions that change the DOM before React hydrates.

- **Official React 19 position (quoted via issue #24430 and the React 19 blog):** React 19 skips unexpected tags in `<head>` and `<body>` rather than raising a mismatch. Stylesheets added by extensions are left in place if React re-renders the document. (Issue #24430 is the source; the blog text is quoted there.)
- **Issue #24430 (facebook/react, 2022):** A browser plugin that inserted a script tag before `<head>` produced a hydration mismatch that broke the UI. The reporter asked whether React could handle this case in its matching logic. The issue is marked as backlog.
- **Issue #25924 (facebook/react, 2022):** The React DevTools extension injected a script after `<body>`, causing occasional hydration errors in React 18.2 when the whole document was rendered from `<html>`. The reporter asked whether the extension should add `suppressHydrationWarning` to that script.
- **Issue #36169 (facebook/react, March 2026):** A `<script defer>` inside `<head>` triggers hydration errors on React 19.2.4. The cause is unclear. The thread also notes that React's own hydration-mismatch message lists browser extensions as a possible cause.
- **Issue #35210 (facebook/react, Nov 2025):** A Mantine-based app on React 19.2.0 hit random hydration errors during navigation. The thread points to React's guidance that extensions can alter HTML before hydration.
- **Next.js discussion #72035:** A ColorZilla attribute (`cz-shortcut-listen`) caused a mismatch on React 19 RC. Disabling the extension fixed it. One user wrote a MutationObserver-based workaround that strips the attribute before hydration. Another commenter reported that a Vue DevTools extension caused similar problems.
- **Video Speed Controller issue #1255 (igrigorik/videospeed):** The extension added an attribute to the `<html>` element that broke hydration in Next.js. The maintainers did not treat the extension as the fix location, and the thread argues that a denylist would not solve the root problem.
- **Recent PR #26 (suv27/Layer7-Siege, Sept 2026):** The fix was to add `suppressHydrationWarning` to the `<body>` element only, because Grammarly-style attributes were injected there.

Overall, the threads show that React 19 tolerates some extension changes in `<head>` and `<body>`, but attributes added to other elements still cause mismatches. The common workarounds are disabling the extension, suppressing the warning on the affected element, or removing the injected attribute before hydration. I did not open the threads, so the details come only from search snippets, and some threads may have been updated since.

content.text:
Yes. Several threads cover this. I only read search snippets and didn't open the issues, so check the details yourself.

**Closest matches in facebook/react**
- [#25924: Scripts injected by browser extensions (e.g. React DevTools) may cause hydration errors](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924) is about React 18.2. An extension-injected script after `<body>` caused hydration errors when the whole document was rendered from `<html>`.
- [#24430: Hydration mismatch error due to plugins generating script tag on top](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/24430) is the older, broader report of the same problem. React 19 is reported to skip unexpected tags in `<head>` and `<body>`, which would address this case.
- [#36169: Hydration mismatch on `<script defer>` rendered inside `<head>`](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/36169) is a React 19.2.4 report. I couldn't tell from the snippet whether an extension is the cause.
- [#35210: A tree hydrated but some attributes of the server rendered HTML didn't match](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/35210) is a React 19.2.0 report. It points to extensions as a possible cause.

**React 19 specifically**
- [Next.js discussion #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035) covers a React 19 RC hydration error caused by the ColorZilla extension adding a `cz-shortcut-listen="true"` attribute. It includes workarounds.

I found no single canonical React 19 issue titled "browser extensions cause hydration mismatch". React 19 tolerates extension changes in `<head>` and `<body>`. Extension-added attributes on other elements, such as `<html>`, still cause mismatches. The usual workarounds are disabling the extension, adding `suppressHydrationWarning` on the affected element, or stripping the attribute before hydration.
